title: DSP pedagogy proposal: executable systems, measurements, and implementation departures
course_throughline: Samples acquire meaning through units and sampling assumptions; LTI structure makes them predictable; Fourier coordinates make behavior measurable and computable; finite records force statistical and time-frequency tradeoffs; filters become trustworthy only under implementation constraints; multirate, communication, and compression systems succeed only when alias, reconstruction, word-length, rate, and latency budgets close together.

governing_rules.L2: Use 27 substantial lessons rather than micro-lessons; target 30–40 minutes where derivation and boundary cases warrant it.
governing_rules.L10: Each lesson is one move in the stated five-module argument; every lesson record below names its inherited problem and handoff.
governing_rules.L15: Reserve callouts for assumptions, failure boundaries, or consequences that prose alone would not preserve; never box a restatement.
governing_rules.L16: Every module ends in a real artifact or runnable study with named module results and an ideal-versus-implementation comparison.
governing_rules.E6: Every set includes at least a boundary probe, a claim to refute, and a derivation or research-shaped task; at most one plug-in warm-up.
governing_rules.E7: Every lesson has a forward exercise that computes or encounters the next lesson's object before it is named.
governing_rules.D1: Only the fifteen demos below are proposed; each has a learner target, numerical threshold, and falsification task that needs dynamic or multi-parameter behavior.

lesson_shape.opening: Exact declarative problem statement, followed by a 2–4 sentence throughline placement.
lesson_shape.body: Concrete case or formal definition as appropriate; derivation; worked example; near-isomorphic exercise with fading; implementation failure; verification.
lesson_shape.visuals: Four to six single-idea visuals per lesson in this proposal, roughly one per 3–4 substantive paragraphs; step-through for processes.
lesson_shape.close: Mixed E6 exercise set, explicit E7 handoff, then verified references with section/page pointers.

visual_policy.draw: Use component figures for formulas, pipelines, matrices, multi-panel comparisons, and long labels; use raw SVG only for simple plots; use sequences for algorithms and changing spectra.
visual_policy.source: Use a sourced raster only when the measured or historical artifact itself is evidence. A published explanatory diagram is always redrawn.
visual_policy.rights: A selected capture is not permission. Every source image remains gated by the recorded license; if clearance fails, substitute a newly measured/redistributable artifact, never a traced redraw.
visual_policy.density_check: Every lesson below has 4–6 visual ideas, satisfying the requested 4–8 range.

exercise_policy.worked_pair: Every demonstrated technique receives a near-isomorphic body exercise with a collapsed full solution; multi-step techniques use backward fading.
exercise_policy.end_set: Five to seven exercises: at most one unfamiliar-computation warm-up, then strategy choice, decision-point explanation, error diagnosis, E6 tasks, spaced review, and E7 bridge.
exercise_policy.interleaving: From L13 onward, mix confusable methods without naming them: padding versus longer data, FIR versus IIR, direct versus FFT convolution, direct versus polyphase, magnitude quality versus PR.
exercise_policy.solutions: Show the full path and end with the transferable decision; forward solutions explicitly name and link the next result.

demos.objective: Make nonunique reconstruction and the Nyquist boundary visible under simultaneous frequency, sample-rate, phase, and reconstruction controls.
demos.learner_task: Set the lowest sample rate that reconstructs every tone in a supplied 0–4 kHz mixture, then deliberately choose a tone/phase at the equality boundary that defeats the rule stated without a guard band.
demos.target: Reconstruction error below −60 dB for every test tone.
demos.threshold: Pass only when fs exceeds twice the highest occupied frequency with the supplied transition guard; equality is not accepted as a universal guarantee.
demos.falsification_task: Break the claim 'samples uniquely identify the continuous waveform' by producing two continuous sinusoids with the same displayed samples.
demos.why_D1: Several continuous candidates and spectral replicas change together; a static panel cannot support threshold search or counterexample construction.
demos.execution: Client-side generated sinusoids and FFT; feedback under 200 ms; no network.

demos.objective: Turn convolution from a moving picture into an identification task.
demos.learner_task: Adjust three impulse-response taps until a dry click train matches the observed echo output, then verify the same kernel on a second input.
demos.target: Recover every tap within 0.01 and achieve normalized output error below 1%.
demos.threshold: The second-input validation must pass; fitting only the first input is insufficient.
demos.falsification_task: Construct two different kernels that match a single constant input and use the validation signal to distinguish them.
demos.why_D1: Tap changes alter delay, overlap, waveform, and audio jointly, and the held-out input turns manipulation into model discrimination.
demos.execution: Client-side convolution and Web Audio; no network.

demos.objective: Connect recurrence coefficients, pole radius, transient length, and bounded-output behavior.
demos.learner_task: Tune a second-order resonator to a requested frequency while keeping all poles within radius 0.98 and the 1% settling time under 200 samples.
demos.target: Frequency error below 1%, pole radius at most 0.98, settling-time constraint met.
demos.threshold: Any pole on or outside the unit circle fails even if the displayed finite trace looks bounded.
demos.falsification_task: Find coefficients whose first 100 samples look harmless but whose longer impulse response grows.
demos.why_D1: The deceptive transient length is a parameter-dependent temporal effect; the task requires searching beyond a static pole plot.
demos.execution: Client-side recurrence, pole solver, and plots.

demos.objective: Show why sine and cosine projections are jointly required for phase-independent tone measurement.
demos.learner_task: Estimate an unknown tone's amplitude and phase first with one projection and then with an I/Q pair as the input phase is randomized.
demos.target: Amplitude error below 1% for all phases and phase error below 2 degrees.
demos.threshold: A sine-only detector must fail for at least one phase; the complex detector must pass the full sweep.
demos.falsification_task: Refute 'one matched sinusoid is enough to measure a tone' by finding its null phase.
demos.why_D1: The learner searches a continuous phase family and watches two projections trade energy while magnitude stays invariant.
demos.execution: Client-side dot products with instant phasor/waveform updates.

demos.objective: Separate spectral interpolation from physical resolving power.
demos.learner_task: Use zero padding to reduce a single-tone peak-location error below 0.1 original bins, then try and fail to resolve two tones merged by the unchanged record length.
demos.target: Single-tone estimate within 0.1 bins; correct written verdict on the unresolved pair.
demos.threshold: No padding setting counts as resolving the pair unless two stable maxima remain under a small phase perturbation.
demos.falsification_task: Disprove 'more FFT points increase frequency resolution' while identifying the narrower claim that is true.
demos.why_D1: Padding, record length, separation, and relative phase form a multi-parameter surface with different success criteria.
demos.execution: Client-side FFT; no audio or network required.

demos.objective: Make factorization, operation count, ordering, and numerical equivalence an engineering choice.
demos.learner_task: Choose a mixed-radix plan for N=960, place the reorder stage, and stay under an arithmetic budget while matching the direct DFT on a small validation case.
demos.target: At least 8× fewer complex multiply-adds than direct evaluation and max relative error below 1e−10.
demos.threshold: Plans that omit required permutation or scaling fail numerical validation.
demos.falsification_task: Refute 'FFT means radix 2 and therefore requires a power-of-two record' with a valid factorization.
demos.why_D1: Factor choices alter a plan graph, operation ledger, memory order, and computed output together.
demos.execution: Client-side plan simulator; use small direct DFT only for validation.

demos.objective: Make the resolution–leakage tradeoff operational for unequal nearby tones.
demos.learner_task: Detect a −40 dB tone 5.5 original bins from a strong tone by choosing window and record length before the phase is randomized.
demos.target: Weak peak at least 3 dB above the local leakage floor across all tested relative phases.
demos.threshold: A single favorable phase does not pass; robustness sweep is mandatory.
demos.falsification_task: Refute 'the narrowest main lobe is always the best window' with the rectangular-window failure.
demos.why_D1: Window, length, bin offset, amplitude ratio, and phase jointly decide detection; no single static comparison establishes robustness.
demos.execution: Client-side synthetic two-tone experiment modeled on Harris §VI.

demos.objective: Expose the coupled variance and resolution costs of frame length, overlap, window, and averaging.
demos.learner_task: Configure a Welch estimate that separates tones 0.04 cycles/sample apart while keeping coefficient of variation below 0.30 over repeated noise realizations.
demos.target: Both peak-separation and variability criteria pass over at least 50 seeded trials.
demos.threshold: Extremely short or extremely long segments fail one of the two criteria.
demos.falsification_task: Refute 'a longer raw periodogram becomes stable' by comparing variability at two record lengths without smoothing.
demos.why_D1: The task needs repeated realizations and a Pareto search across several estimator parameters.
demos.execution: Seeded client-side noise and FFT; deterministic replay.

demos.objective: Connect analysis window, hop, overlap sum, and reconstruction error.
demos.learner_task: Choose a window/hop pair that reconstructs a transient-rich signal, then change only the hop until audible/visible modulation appears.
demos.target: Normalized reconstruction error below −100 dB in floating point.
demos.threshold: The overlap-sum deviation must also remain below 1e−10 away from boundaries.
demos.falsification_task: Break the claim '50% overlap always reconstructs' with a window that is not COLA at that hop.
demos.why_D1: The error is periodic in time and depends on coupled window/hop choices; the threshold can be searched and violated.
demos.execution: Client-side STFT/ISTFT and optional Web Audio.

demos.objective: Show that algebraically equivalent IIR structures diverge after coefficient and state quantization.
demos.learner_task: Choose word length and section ordering so a narrowband IIR stays stable and within 0.5 dB of the target response.
demos.target: All quantized poles inside radius 0.999 and max passband error below 0.5 dB.
demos.threshold: Test direct form and cascaded second-order sections under identical bit budgets.
demos.falsification_task: Refute 'equivalent transfer functions imply equivalent implementations' by finding a bit depth where direct form fails and SOS passes.
demos.why_D1: Quantization grids, pole migration, state growth, and response error change nonlinearly with word length and topology.

demos.objective: Turn window choice and tap count into a constrained filter-design problem.
demos.learner_task: Meet 0.1 dB passband ripple and 60 dB stopband attenuation across a fixed transition with the fewest odd taps.
demos.target: All dense-grid specifications pass; minimize tap count within the allowed window/equiripple families.
demos.threshold: Checking only frequency samples used in design does not count; dense verification is required.
demos.falsification_task: Refute 'a longer rectangular truncation removes Gibbs ripple' by tracking peak ripple while transition width shrinks.
demos.why_D1: Tap count, family, transition width, and dense-grid extrema create a search with an explicit optimum.
demos.execution: Client-side FIR design and dense response evaluation.

demos.objective: Make computational savings and exact equivalence visible in a rational converter.
demos.learner_task: Transform a direct L/M converter into a polyphase schedule and match its samples while minimizing executed multiplies.
demos.target: Max output difference below 1e−10 and at most 35% of the direct multiply count for the supplied case.
demos.threshold: Counting multiplies by zero after expansion is treated as executed work and fails the budget.
demos.falsification_task: Refute 'zero insertion followed by high-rate filtering is unavoidable' by showing which phases alone produce each output.
demos.why_D1: The execution schedule changes with output phase and ratio; a static identity does not test whether work was actually removed.
demos.execution: Client-side sample scheduler and operation ledger.

demos.objective: Distinguish channel selectivity from alias cancellation and perfect reconstruction.
demos.learner_task: Tune a two-channel analysis/synthesis bank for reconstruction, then perturb one synthesis coefficient while keeping individual magnitude responses visually similar.
demos.target: Baseline error below −100 dB and alias component below −90 dB.
demos.threshold: After perturbation, identify the first coefficient change that raises reconstruction error above −40 dB.
demos.why_D1: Aliasing terms cancel through coupled branches; parameter perturbation reveals a relationship invisible in separate magnitude plots.
demos.execution: Client-side filter bank on a transient/audio signal.

demos.objective: Connect analytic signals, quadrature mixing, image rejection, and communication error.
demos.learner_task: Correct gain and phase imbalance in a QPSK receiver until the constellation and unwanted image meet limits, then introduce carrier offset.
demos.target: EVM below 5% and image rejection above 40 dB.
demos.threshold: Find and report the phase-imbalance value where EVM first exceeds 10%.
demos.falsification_task: Refute 'real mixing alone isolates one sideband' by measuring the image in the uncorrected receiver.
demos.why_D1: Constellation, spectrum, image, and EVM respond jointly to continuous phase/gain/frequency controls.

demos.objective: Test the additive-white quantization-noise model instead of assuming it.
demos.learner_task: Quantize low-level speech at 3 bits with and without dither and tune dither until error correlation and spectral spurs meet thresholds.
demos.target: Absolute input/error correlation below 0.05 and largest deterministic spur reduced by at least 10 dB.
demos.threshold: Report the SNR cost; a result that hides spurs by muting the signal fails.
demos.falsification_task: Refute 'quantization error is always independent white noise' using the undithered 3-bit record.
demos.why_D1: Signal level, bit depth, dither distribution, correlation, spectrum, and audio quality must be balanced across real samples.
demos.execution: Client-side quantizer and seeded dither; bundled rights-cleared speech.

applications.artifact_or_study: Perching-glider flight data: measured lift/drag coefficients versus angle of attack and the recorded approach trajectory.
executable_protocol: Load a provenance-preserving, redistributable CSV of flight-test samples; retain a held-out contiguous maneuver.
Fit a flat-plate baseline and one low-order data model; plot residuals against angle of attack and time.
Use the model in a discrete recurrence to predict the held-out maneuver; report train/test error separately.
Locate the stall region where the ideal theory departs systematically from measurements.
applications.target_and_threshold: Reduce held-out RMSE by at least 20% relative to the flat-plate baseline without increasing model order after viewing the test set.
applications.falsification_task: Test and reject, if warranted, 'a higher-order polynomial is necessarily the better flight model' using held-out error and residual structure.
applications.ideal_vs_implementation: Flat-plate theory assumes an idealized aerodynamic regime; the measured scatter, stall nonlinearity, sensor noise, finite sampling, and controller delay violate it.
applications.deliverable: Reproducible notebook/browser report with model equation, residual plot, validation metric, and one paragraph naming the idealization gap.
applications.data_gate: Do not digitize the published plot as data. Bundle original numeric data only under verified rights; otherwise select a separately licensed flight dataset.

applications.artifact_or_study: A deployed dual-tone telephone signaling receiver tested through a real loudspeaker/microphone or supplied channel recording.
executable_protocol: Generate the standard row/column tone pairs and pass them through a recorded or browser-simulated phone channel.
Build a fixed-latency detector using FFT bins or matched complex correlations; do not identify the method in the final mixed test.
Sweep noise, frequency offset, amplitude twist, and key duration; produce a confusion matrix.
Compare direct correlations and FFT computation at the chosen block size.
applications.target_and_threshold: At least 99% accuracy on clean keys and 95% at 10 dB SNR with ±1.5% frequency offset, using no more than 40 ms decision latency.
applications.falsification_task: Refute 'more zero padding always fixes two-tone decisions' by holding record duration fixed while changing only FFT length.
applications.ideal_vs_implementation: Orthogonal bin-centered sinusoids become off-bin, unequal, noisy, reverberant, and time-limited in a real acoustic/telephone path.
applications.deliverable: Receiver code, threshold table, confusion matrix, failure example, and arithmetic/latency budget.
applications.data_gate: The browser may record the learner's own tones locally; provide a small redistributable channel corpus for reproducibility.

applications.artifact_or_study: Recorded oboe, speech, and piano analyses comparing leakage, peak estimation, Welch stability, STFT resolution, and phase-aware resynthesis.
executable_protocol: Use one rights-cleared isolated note and one utterance; publish exact sample rate, frame length, window, hop, and FFT length.
Predict which weak harmonics each window will reveal before computing the spectra.
Estimate fundamental/partials and repeat across adjacent frames; compare raw periodogram and Welch variability.
Compute two spectrogram parameterizations and one magnitude-only versus phase-preserving reconstruction.
applications.target_and_threshold: Stable voiced-frequency estimates within 1% across adjacent frames, and reconstruction error below −80 dB for the phase-preserving COLA path; every claimed harmonic must persist under a neighboring-frame check.
applications.falsification_task: Reject 'the plot with the most FFT bins has the best physical resolution' using fixed-data padding and longer-data comparisons.
applications.ideal_vs_implementation: Stationary sinusoids, white noise, exact bin centering, and perfect COLA are approximations; attacks, vibrato, formant motion, colored noise, and finite frames break them.
applications.deliverable: Parameter ledger, matched spectrum panels, variability statistics, reconstruction check, and listening files.
applications.data_gate: Published plots require rights review. If not cleared, use the same protocol on CC-licensed recordings; never redraw measured curves.

applications.artifact_or_study: A real ECG with baseline drift, cardiac content, broadband noise, and narrow 60 Hz interference.
executable_protocol: Inspect a redistributable ECG record in time and frequency; set preservation and rejection bands before designing.
Build a baseline-removal stage, 60 Hz notch, and high-frequency lowpass; compare FIR and IIR alternatives.
Measure QRS peak change, group delay, settling/ringing, 60 Hz attenuation, and fixed-point stability.
Process by direct filtering and block convolution where applicable; confirm block boundaries do not add artifacts.
applications.target_and_threshold: Suppress 60 Hz by at least 30 dB and baseline drift by at least 20 dB while changing QRS peak amplitudes by less than 5%; no quantized pole may reach radius 1.
applications.falsification_task: Refute 'the magnitude response alone determines the better medical filter' with delay/ringing and morphology evidence.
applications.ideal_vs_implementation: Ideal brick-wall separation is impossible because diagnostic content and noise overlap; finite delay, edge transients, coefficient rounding, and morphology preservation constrain the design.
applications.deliverable: Filter cascade, dense response, before/after trace and spectrum, morphology metric, transient analysis, and word-length decision.
applications.data_gate: Use a verified redistributable ECG record for computation; the MIT artifact may be shown only under its stated license.

applications.artifact_or_study: A local streaming audio link that resamples 48 kHz to 44.1 kHz, splits into subbands, quantizes under a bit budget, transmits I/Q symbols, and reconstructs.
executable_protocol: Record or load rights-cleared 48 kHz audio and implement the 441/480 converter both directly and polyphase.
Split into a PR bank, estimate subband variances, allocate bits under a 96 kb/s payload budget, and packetize.
Map payload to QPSK, add a controlled channel impairment, recover, synthesize, and restore 44.1 kHz audio.
Measure alias rejection, reconstruction error, EVM, rate, operation count, latency, and listening artifacts.
applications.target_and_threshold: Polyphase/direct output difference below 1e−10 in floating point, out-of-band aliases below −70 dB, baseline PR error below −100 dB, channel EVM below 5%, payload at or below 96 kb/s, and end-to-end latency below 100 ms.
applications.falsification_task: Test 'perfect reconstruction in exact algebra guarantees perfect deployed reconstruction' by quantizing analysis and synthesis coefficients independently, then repair the structure.
applications.ideal_vs_implementation: Infinite filters, exact rational clocks, independent white quantization noise, exact PR coefficients, synchronized carriers, and zero packet delay do not survive finite buffers and fixed-point transport.
applications.deliverable: Runnable link, rate/latency/operation ledger, spectra and constellation, reconstruction metrics, and one audible failure/repair pair.
applications.data_gate: Use learner-owned or CC-licensed audio; the published quantization plots are optional evidence pending publisher review.

modules.title: Discrete signals and systems
modules.argument: A sampled record becomes predictable only after units, system memory, sampling assumptions, and stability are explicit.
spiral_revisits: sample rate and units recur in every later spectrum
convolution returns in filtering, STFT, and polyphase systems
stability returns under IIR and fixed point

modules.title: Fourier representation and computation
modules.argument: Complex modes diagonalize LTI behavior; finite coordinates and factorization turn that representation into a receiver.
spiral_revisits: phase returns in STFT and I/Q links
DFT scaling returns in PSD and fast convolution
FFT cost returns in every streaming design

modules.title: Spectral measurement
modules.argument: Finite and random records require explicit tradeoffs among leakage, resolution, variance, time localization, and reconstruction.
spiral_revisits: windows return in FIR and filter banks

modules.title: Filters under implementation constraints
modules.argument: Pole-zero designs are engineering objects only after order, phase, transients, blocks, topology, and finite precision are verified.
spiral_revisits: sampling guard bands constrain every filter
FFT and convolution reappear in block filtering
stability is re-tested after coefficient quantization

modules.title: Multirate communications and compression
modules.argument: Rate changes, channel decompositions, quadrature transport, and bit allocation reduce cost only when aliasing and reconstruction remain controlled in finite arithmetic.
spiral_revisits: sampling and convolution become noble identities
DFT/filter-bank duality unifies spectra and channels

lessons.title: Sampled sequences and physical units
lessons.goal: Represent a measured waveform as a discrete sequence with correct index, time, amplitude, and rate units.
lessons.throughline: The course begins with the data object every later system will transform; nothing between samples is silently assumed.
lessons.implementation_gap: A numeric array omits analog bandwidth, clock jitter, calibration, clipping, and the reconstruction rule.
